rationale: This empirical organizational sociology study tests the psychometric dimensionality of R. Hall's model of bureaucracy using questionnaires and interviews of nurses across six general hospitals in the Netherlands. It has no connection to water or sanitation service access (failing Criterion 1 and Criterion 4) and is excluded as wrong topic (E01).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Although internal hospital bureaucracy and organizational rules/procedures fall within generic administrative/institutional concepts under the literal Criterion 2 wording, the study is completely unrelated to household or community water or sanitation service access and measures psychometric properties of Hall's bureaucracy scale rather than any service access outcome, so it is excluded under both readings.

evidence_quotes.quote: Bureaucracy in the Hospital: An Empirical Test of Hall's Theory in One Organizational Type
In a study of 6 general hospitals in the Netherlands, R. Hall's dimensional model of bureaucracy was tested for its applicability within one type of organization.
Nurses (number of cases = 442) representing 31 departments in 6 hospitals were interviewed.
